arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4827] why am I being logged out every time I switch machines?
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

I'm sorry for the disruption—especially on a deadline. 

Based on our latest documentation, there has been no change in Cursor’s sign-in policy: signing in with Google SSO should allow multiple simultaneous sessions across different devices, and billing-related device verification does not affect normal sign-in sessions.

If you’re being logged out every time you move between machines, that is not expected behavior. There are no documented policy changes that would cause this. This may be a recent bug affecting account sessions, especially with Google SSO.

To help the support team investigate further (and to prevent more lost work), please provide any relevant details:
- All device types and browsers used, and if you notice it after any particular action/sequence.
- Whether you’ve recently changed your Google account password or settings.

Meanwhile, you might try clearing your browser cache/cookies or using a private/incognito window as a quick test, but this is likely a server-side issue.

If you need this escalated urgently for log review, please reply with any additional details. I will also flag this directly with the support team.

Thank you for your patience,
Lyra Support Bot

[Source: sso-google-signin.md, payment-method-device-binding.md]

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4815] Invoice PDF won't download
arguments.body:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for reaching out. When an invoice PDF fails to download (the button just spins), it may be due to a temporary server glitch or a browser-side caching issue. Here’s what you can try:

1. Refresh your browser and try again, or use a private/incognito window.
2. Make sure third-party cookies are allowed for billing.cursor.com.
3. Try downloading from a different device or network, in case there’s a local or firewall restriction.

If the issue persists, this might require a support engineer to check the logs and send the PDF manually. Please reply and mention your account email, browser (Chrome, Safari, etc.), and date/time of your latest attempt—we’ll escalate promptly if it’s still stuck.

Thanks for your patience,
Lyra Support Bot

[Source: payment-method-device-binding.md, contact-human-support.md]

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4820] Feature request: keyboard shortcut for inline edit
arguments.body:
Hi Riya,

Thank you for your suggestion and for outlining your workflow. As of now, there isn’t a dedicated keyboard shortcut for triggering inline edit directly in Cursor—you’re correct that cmd-K, then clicking, is the current method.

Your request is appreciated and I’ll pass this on to our product team for visibility. If this feature gets prioritized, updates will be posted in the release notes or the Help Center.

Thanks again for your input and for using Cursor!
Lyra Support Bot

[Source: internal documentation review]
